newsitem.title: EGYPT: Moussa declines to confirm Cairo summit conditions.
newsitem.headline: Moussa declines to confirm Cairo summit conditions.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa distanced Cairo on Tuesday from any specific conditions Israel must meet for a Middle East economic conference to go ahead in Cairo in November.

The Egyptian ambassador to Israel, Mohammed Bassiouny, said on Monday that Egypt was giving Israel three weeks to start carrying out several steps -- redeploying from Hebron and other parts of the West Bank, opening safe passages between Gaza and the West Bank, releasing all Palestinian women prisoners and lifting the closure of Palestinian territories.
Moussa, asked to confirm these conditions, said: "I was told about this (what Bassiouny said) but I have not seen the exact words. Let us not talk about conditions."

But the minister repeated his view that there would have to be visible progress towards peace otherwise public opinion would react against the economic conference, which is meant to help integrate Israel into the regional economy.

"Just imagine we are now sitting in the conference talking about future cooperation and how prosperity should prevail... while there is no progress at all in the peace process itself. So public opinion will lose credibility and there will be a backlash instead of something that will benefit us," he said.

"We emphasise our commitment to reach a peace that would bring Israel into the Middle East family of nations. Everybody, all parties, will have to pay for that, including Israel. There is no free lunch, neither for us or for Israel," he added.
